title: RBAC v2 replay engine + middleware inspector for runtime & console
creator: Asha Menon
description: Build a low-latency "replay engine" and lightweight middleware inspector to support RBAC v2 policy evaluation across the public API runtime and the admin console. The replay engine will allow deterministic re-evaluation of historical authorization decisions (for audits, incident forensics, and policy tuning) while the middleware inspector provides per-request explainability and trace correlation without adding tail latency to live inference traffic. This ticket scopes the core engine, middleware adapters for HTTP/gRPC, audit-log enrichment, SAML/SSO admin mapping hooks, and the console inspector UI surface required by compliance and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Replay engine can re-evaluate a recorded request (headers + principal + resource) against the active RBAC v2 policy set and produce a decision + reasoning within a bounded time (median <= 30ms on CPU node).

Middleware inspector can attach a compact decision-token to live requests that the console can fetch for debugging without blocking request completion (inspect endpoint returns decision and compact derivation trace).

Audit pipeline enhancements: every decision emitted includes policy revision id, compiled-policy-hash, principal source (SSO/SAML mapping if present), and a stable request-replay blob stored in the audit-sink.
End-to-end test demonstrating replay of a failed allow/deny after policy change, with traceable drift identified by policy-hash mismatch alerts.
Security review completed and SAML admin attribute mapping documented in the runbook.
technical_notes: Policy compilation: compile RBAC v2 rules to a sandboxed WASM representation to allow fast CPU replays and memory-friendly caches.
Eval model: runtime uses a fast-indexed predicate evaluator with a small pre-filter index (subject/resource/action) to avoid scanning full rule sets on replay.
KV cache: keep a tiny MRU cache of compiled-policy-wasm per-tenant; eviction policy tuned to keep hottest 1000 tenants on control plane nodes.

Middleware adapter: provide pluggable hooks for HTTP (Express/gateway) and gRPC interceptors to emit decision-tokens; interceptor must be non-blocking and attach token via response header X-RBAC-Trace.

Audit format: use newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with fields: timestamp, request_id, principal_id, principal_source, policy_revision, compiled_policy_hash, decision, reason_tokens (array), replay_blob_s3_key.
SSO/SAML: map SAML attributes -> internal roles during admin console session establishment; provide fallback when mapping absent and log mapping misses to audit stream.
Console inspector: read-only UI widget that fetches decision-token details from a read-replica audit index and displays an abbreviated derivation trace and policy snippet links.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy replay engine as a sidecar on a subset of control-plane nodes; enable middleware inspector in read-only mode for non-critical routes.
Phase 2 (limited): enable decision-token emission for staging and selected customer orgs; start shipping enriched audit events to internal audit-sink in staging.
Phase 3 (broad): enable for all non-latency-critical paths; monitor tail-latency and error budget closely; toggle via runtime feature flag.
Phase 4: once metrics stable, enable decision-token for admin console and provide UI inspector to SRE and support roles behind RBAC.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy WASM compilation: verify semantic equivalence between interpreter and compiled outputs on canonical policy corpus.
Integration tests for replay: record 1000 synthetic requests, mutate policy set, replay and assert expected drift metrics and replay latency distribution.
Performance tests: CPU-only replay benchmark with 95th percentile < 100ms for 99% of replays under 8k QPS synthetic load.
Security tests: fuzz SAML attribute mappings and ensure missing/invalid attributes are rejected and logged; run threat model review on replay storage.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: WASM cold-starts for large policy sets could add latency. Mitigation: pre-warm compiled images and use lazy JIT warm paths; measure cold-start percentiles during canary.
Risk: Replay blobs may contain sensitive PII. Mitigation: redact sensitive fields before storing; provide per-tenant opt-out and KMS encryption for storage.

Risk: Emitting decision tokens could leak internal policy details. Mitigation: token contains only references and abbreviated derivation (no full rules); access-controlled fetch endpoint for inspector UI.
Risk: SAML attribute mapping ambiguity causing privilege mis-mapping. Mitigation: require explicit claim-to-role mappings during enterprise onboarding; log and alert mapping misses.
notes: Spike completed: prototype WASM compile path and a small interpreter comparison (Asha, 2026-03-08).
Blocked on infra quota for additional CPU nodes for canary; infra request opened (#INFRA-1324).
PM asked to prioritize console inspector visibility for SRE use-cases--we will expose a compact decision-token first and iterate on UI.
We decided to avoid shipping full policy text in audit events to reduce risk surface; audit contains policy references and hashes.
Plan to coordinate with compliance to document retention window and redaction rules before enabling cross-tenant replay storage.
